The environmental impact of an AFES for vehicles above 6,000 pounds GVWR that produced the same percentage improvement in fuel economy as this AFES is likely to be slightly greater than the impact of this AFES assuming that the same fuel economy improvement measures are used for the heavier vehicles. Thus, for the total fleet of vehicles of no more than 10,000 pounds GVWR the environmental impact would be slightly greater than twice the impact of this AFES.
c. Extend the AFES to include MY 1980 and beyond. Concern about market shifts could cause a conservative approach to establishing standards for subsequent years unless NPA's above 6,000 pounds GVWR are also regulated. The concern about market shifts arises because unregulated vehicles above 6,000 pounds GVWR unburdened by possible reduction in performance, or increases in price due to fuel economy measures, have lower fuel economy than vehicles less than 6,000 pounds GVWR. If actions required to meet the AFES result in vehicles which the buyer perceives as not meeting his needs, the manufacturer or the consumer could shift to vehicles over 6,000 pounds GVWR, thereby defeating the intent of the AFES.
